title: The hub key files' mount mode conflicts with the hub loader
remediation: The site stack's hub chart (deploy/hub) mounted the hub's TLS, signing and encryption key files from its Secrets with mode 0440, and the hub's loader (hub/src/secrets.ts) refuses any key file that group or others can read, so a hub on the site cluster would stop at start. Kubernetes cannot give a non-root user an owner-only Secret file: the kubelet writes Secret files owned by root and, under the pod's fsGroup, makes each one at least 0440 whatever defaultMode says (the user fields of KEP-5936 are alpha in Kubernetes 1.37 and leave the fsGroup bits). The chart now copies the files in an init container, the hub image's own Node running deploy/hub/files/stage-secrets.cjs as the hub's user 65532, into a memory volume where each is created 0400 and owned by 65532, and the hub reads only those copies; the loader's rule is unchanged. deploy/test/render-stateful.test.mjs checks that the chart runs that file as the hub's user and points every HUB_*_FILE setting at the copies, and hub/test/secrets.test.ts runs the file on a Secret volume laid out as the kubelet writes it and loads the copies with the hub's loader. Neither has run on a cluster. This closes when a hub on the lab cluster (RKE2 v1.37) has started and the record shows each file under /run/secrets/hub in the running pod as 0400 and owned by 65532, and the hub's secrets.loaded line.

milestones.title: Start a hub on Phase 48's lab-full rig and record the mode and owner of each file under /run/secrets/hub in the running pod and the hub's secrets.loaded line
